color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
On claim, code walks the graph. No model compiles the packet
Agents read the database through tools, never the Markdown export
More context is worse. Critical items go at the start
A short checklist of the same rules goes at the end

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Goal, write scope, contract versions, spec items, in-scope rules,
edge cases, visible examples, the interaction contract, definition of done
If Must alone exceeds the model, the planner splits the task
It is never truncated. About 2 to 3k tokens for a Junior, 4 to 6k for a Senior

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Convention lines for the files, library warnings,
signatures of accepted dependencies, tokens and kit pieces for UI

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Neighbor summaries, rationale, full research. Pull only

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A cross-cutting rule has a scope predicate, not a home document
The task declares routes, entities, screens, libraries and layers
Every rule is matched. A sign-up rule reaches an export that touches names
An architect's local rule that is really cross-cutting must be moved,
or marked local with a reason
Each in-scope rule names checks. Acceptance fails if those checks did not pass

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
kb.search, kb.get, kb.neighbors, kb.contract, kb.why, kb.code
Full text first. Embeddings are optional
Call and token limits per attempt. Responses are data, not instructions
A miss becomes AskOwner. A real gap becomes a spec item
A revision pins the brief's version. Newest is opt-in

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Declared dependency. If it changes: hold at the next boundary
and refresh the brief

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Observed dependency. At acceptance, recheck
A material change reruns verification on the new version

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Pulls are recorded by task class and whether the task passed
Weekly, the meta-lab may propose pushing a repeatedly pulled item
A predicate that lands in most packets, with no related failures,
is flagged so the architect can narrow it
A diff that touches more than the plan declared adds those facts,
and their checks, before acceptance

svg.text: The packet a task receives, and what it may pull
